solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It bodes ill making potato salad

parts.note: murphy is an old slang word for a potato, from its link with Ireland
slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A cook warns that a particular potato salad recipe is bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' just joins the definition to the wordplay. MURPHY is old Irish-flavoured slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The adage that whatever can go wrong will go wrong is an ominous rule, one that bodes ill for any plan.

clue.text: Extra second added on

indicators.note: added says the next piece is attached after the first one

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: An extra second has been tacked onto the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean additional, as in asking for extra or more helpings.

clue.text: Enterprise, maybe, I managed to secure from Moscow?

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the word for managed holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
USS Enterprise is the starship in Star Trek; USS is the prefix of a United States ship, and 'maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A question about whether a business venture was set up with money from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' reads as a business, but it is the starship, giving USS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming from Moscow is from Russia's capital, so it can be described by the national adjective.

clue.text: Strike bowler's aim to secure win no better?

parts.note: to hit is to strike
in lawn bowls the jack is the small white ball the bowlers aim at
to pot is to secure or bag, as in potting a ball or potting game

explanation.surface: A sportsman muses on how best to win, by hitting the target the bowler is aiming for.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls, a game common on English greens, players roll balls towards a small target ball called the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning the jackpot is the biggest prize available, so it is a win that could not be bettered; an idiom for great success.

clue.text: Who's teasingly left clothes hanging up?

definitions.text: Who's teasingly left clothes hanging up?

indicators.note: teasing out the letters of a word separates and rearranges them, so the four letters are shuffled
in a down answer, hanging up means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A riddle about which performer teasingly left her costume hanging up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teasingly' shuffles WHO'S into SHOW; 'hanging up' turns RIG into GIR in this down entry; L for left ends it. The whole clue also describes a stage performer who strips teasingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in a revue who teasingly sheds her costume fits the whole question; she is a stage performer of that kind.

clue.text: Sets off with top farewell

indicators.note: 'off with top' means the head letter is cut off, like 'off with his head'

parts.note: radios are wireless sets

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey, waving goodbye with a top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets off' reads as departing, but 'Sets' are radio sets and 'off with top' beheads them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for goodbye is widely used in English as a casual farewell.

clue.text: China and gypsum in green banks

indicators.note: the letters lie on the banks where the words meet: the end of one word, the little word, and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A description of porcelain made of gypsum, set among green riverbanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle three words: the final letter of 'gypsum', the word 'in', and the opening letter of 'green'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty's name is used for its prized porcelain, so it means fine china from that era.

clue.text: One tops writer in winter sports location

parts.note: an icer is one who tops cakes with icing
ink is what a pen writes with, so it can stand for a writer

explanation.surface: A single famous name outranks a writer at a ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One tops' looks like 'a single person beats', but it is someone who ices cakes; 'in' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen arena where people skate or play hockey is a venue for winter sports.

clue.text: Win gnome in dispute

parts.note: to gain is to win
a gnome is also a pithy maxim or saying, related to 'gnomic'

explanation.surface: Someone wins a garden gnome in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' is not a garden ornament but the old word for an aphorism; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Contradicting or denying something is the act of disputing it, an old literary synonym.

clue.text: Dish is blue with trim of gold from the East

indicators.note: a trim is an edging, so the gold forms a border wrapped round the other letters
in an across answer, coming from the East means read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
blue means risque or indecent, and OTT (over the top) is used for something excessive or near the knuckle

explanation.surface: A plate is blue with a gilded rim, in an Oriental style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' reads the heraldic gold backwards in this across entry, and 'with trim of' makes it a border; 'blue' is the risque sense, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice preparation cooked slowly in stock is a well-known dish.

clue.text: Executed British leader of Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the first letter of the leader's name is cut off

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A news line about a British leader of a Middle Eastern country being executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something belonging to the state whose capital is Jerusalem, a Middle Eastern nation.

clue.text: Check for binder giving strength

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
cement binds bricks or stones together

explanation.surface: A builder checks a binding agent for its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Added support that makes a structure or force sturdier is extra strength.

clue.text: Having negotiated pub's top shelf?

parts.note: the bottles of whisky, gin and other strong drink sit high up behind the bar, so someone who has worked through them is elated, literally among the elevated liquor

explanation.walkthrough: The top shelf behind a British pub bar usually holds the spirit bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinker who has made it through the strong liquor kept up high is merry, cheerful and elated.

clue.text: One blindly charging for chore irons pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rushes at housework, saying ironing is pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. 'Pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means rubbish, and it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The large horned animal with poor eyesight famously charges at anything in its way.

clue.text: Badly wanting to caress Juliet with uniform on, do they come back at ten to two?

definitions.text: do they come back at ten to two?

indicators.note: to caress is to hold lovingly, so the word for wanting holds the next pieces

parts.note: badly wanting food is being hungry

indicators.note: on says the second letter is placed after the first one

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lovesick admirer longs to embrace Juliet in her uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: A jury that cannot agree keeps returning to court, perhaps at ten to two after lunch, to report no verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel of jurors unable to reach a verdict is sent back out again and again.

clue.text: Jarring striking opener

parts.note: workers who are striking are off work
a key opens a lock

explanation.surface: A batsman's jarring blow as he opens the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A note out of tune is unpleasant to hear; figuratively out of place or discordant.

clue.text: Signal like Holyfield after Tyson had finished snacking

parts.words: like Holyfield after Tyson had finished snacking
parts.note: in 1997 Mike Tyson bit off part of Evander Holyfield's ear, leaving him half-eared: semi plus otic, the adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: A reference to the notorious boxing bout in which Tyson bit Holyfield's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SEMI (half) and OTIC (of the ear): Holyfield was left partly eared.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to signs and signalling, the study of meaning carried by symbols.

clue.text: Sign for steam/water?

parts.note: steam and liquid water are the forms of H2O that are not frozen; read as two words the answer describes them

explanation.surface: A puzzled request for a symbol meaning steam or water.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into NOT ICE, a fair description of steam or water.
explanation.definitionFit: A posted announcement or placard is a sign, as in a notice on a board.

clue.text: After time, get laid up

parts.note: someone laid up in bed is sick, or ailing

explanation.surface: Advice that after a while you will get laid up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a mere sequence word, but it is the definition: being after someone is following them.
explanation.definitionFit: Following someone closely, as police do a suspect, is being after them.

clue.text: Swimmer's ground-breaking power

indicators.note: breaking into the word for ground, the next letter splits it

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Praise for a swimmer's ground-breaking strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground-breaking' looks like one adjective, but it says P breaks into the word for ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is an animal that swims.

clue.text: Get ready to settle

parts.note: ready (readies) is slang for banknotes, so to settle a bill using ready money is the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get ready' reads as 'prepare', but 'ready' is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling a debt in notes and coins rather than by cheque or card is the act described.

clue.text: What speaker aims for consignment of chips from America?

definitions.meaning: a public speaker hopes for a clear, sharp style of speaking
Americans call potato crisps chips, so a shipment of them is a load of crisps

explanation.walkthrough: 'from America' signals the US sense of chips, which the British call crisps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp articulation is the orator's goal; a shipment of packets of thin fried potato slices is the other sense.

clue.text: Greyish at table for breakfast before 7am?

parts.note: Earl Grey is a tea drunk at breakfast; the nobleman's title plus a suffix meaning 'like' gives a word for resembling that tea

explanation.surface: A grey-haired person at the breakfast table before seven.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey is a bergamot-flavoured tea, so EARL plus -Y (like) is 'Grey-ish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Before seven in the morning is at an hour well ahead of the usual time.

clue.text: It's frightful leaving China in the wings

indicators.note: leaving means the porcelain's name departs from the longer word

parts.note: something frightful is alarming
Ming is the Chinese dynasty, and its porcelain is fine china

explanation.surface: A frightful scene: someone leaves China while waiting in the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or shaped like wings, a technical biology term.

clue.text: Amongst duty personnel, see one swagger

indicators.note: amongst places the next piece within the list of names

parts.note: a roster lists the people on duty
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Among the staff on duty, watch one person strutting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave in a noisy, boisterous, swaggering way is an old verb for rowdy revelling.

clue.text: Digital cover

parts.note: digital here means relating to a digit, a toe; the horny plate protecting the end of a toe covers it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but a digit is also a finger or toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard plate on the tip of a toe protects that digit, a covering for it.

clue.text: Chief no more? Long story!

indicators.note: 'no more' says the word for more is taken away from the chief's title

parts.note: a sagamore is a chief among some Native American peoples of New England

explanation.surface: A deposed chief's life is a long story.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norse epic or any lengthy, involved tale counts as a long story.

clue.text: One stunning artist about one year back

indicators.note: about means the artist goes round the other letters

parts.note: an etcher is an artist who makes etched prints

indicators.note: back says the pieces for one and year are read in reverse order

parts.note: an ace is a one on a playing card or die

explanation.surface: A stunning artist went back about a year ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ACE plus Y to make YECA, which goes after the first letter of the printmaker; 'One stunning' is the definition, the second 'one' is the ace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking that grabs attention is a stunning thing to look at.
